title: Do-Calculus with d-Separation for Affine Stochastic Differential Equation Models
banked_reason: D0.5 cold tier subfield is below the field floor: paper-score ceiling 7.0 < 7.4, salvageable=false, and no bounded improvement directive.
gap_reasons: The result proves all three rules for the finite-horizon real-affine positive-diagonal class with product initials and exogenous selectors, but resolves only a structurally narrow subclass of the broader Boeken--Mooij obstruction and provides one strict identification witness.

The supplied Theorem 7.19 attestation gives an equivalence density under its path-integral hypotheses, but not the stated multidimensional two-sided Beneš formulation or the KL identity; state and discharge the precise entropy theorem (or derive the expectation/integrability step) used by the kernel-TV proof.

The supplied Appendix-E passage supplies a factorization in its intervention argument, not the claimed general jointly measurable regular-conditional-kernel theorem for arbitrary standard-Borel indexed kernels; cite or prove that measurable disintegration result used in the transfer lemma.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 constructed all three whole-path d-separation do-calculus rules for a finite-horizon real-affine cyclic SDE class, using fixed-space selector kernels, exact-copy Euler DAGs, grouped trail projection, fibrewise Girsanov/TV convergence, and a strict Rule-2 witness beyond sigma-separation. The class was broadened to arbitrary real affine coefficients and arbitrary independent product initial laws, but cold review still rated the contribution subfield with a 7.0 score ceiling below the 7.4 field floor and no bounded in-scope improvement. A future re-raise would need a materially broader nonlinear or nondiagonal program and must also prove or precisely source the two underspecified Girsanov/KL and measurable-disintegration leaves.
tldr: All three whole-path do-calculus rules hold with d-separation for finite-horizon real affine systems with strictly positive diagonal diffusion, arbitrary independent product initial laws independent of the Brownian noise, and arbitrary dependent selector laws exogenous to those variables. The square-integrable-initial subfamily is the real-affine positive-diagonal subclass of Boeken--Mooij Assumption 2; the proof itself needs no initial moment condition because its moment bounds are conditional on each fixed initial value and the final mixing step uses only a unit total-variation bound. Jointly Borel exact and Euler kernels, grouped-grid projection, fibrewise Girsanov convergence, total-variation transfer, and selector disintegration yield all three rules. A five-coordinate rational Hurwitz system gives a legal Rule 2 case in which d-separation holds and sigma-separation fails. No nonlinear or arbitrary-invertible-diffusion extension is asserted.
gap: Boeken–Mooij prove the additive-noise observational d-Markov theorem and, separately, a sigma-separation do-calculus using path-valued intervention variables. On p. 25, Section 8.2 they explicitly leave the d-separation do-calculus open because the augmented intervention system falls outside the proved additive-noise class. A bounded search through 22 September 2026 found no public resolution.
fill: Prove essential solvability, fixed-space jointly Borel exact and Euler kernels, the exact selector-mixture TV inequality, the two-selector grouped projection, TV transfer of selector conditional independences, and the Appendix-E disintegration for all three rules; then certify one continuous-path Rule-2 case that is d-separated but not sigma-separated.
